Kernel-Bypass Edge Packet Scheduling for High-Throughput IoT Gateways

Director at IIJ Research Lab with unmatched access to live global network edge measurement feeds

publications.title: Benchmarking methodology for stateful NAT64 gateways
publications.research_problem: Standard network benchmarking methodologies have conflicting requirements when applied to stateful NAT64 gateways.
publications.approach: A benchmarking methodology for any stateful NATxy gateway that reconciles those requirements and defines new stateful metrics.
publications.key_contribution: New metrics (connection establishment rate, tear-down rate, connection-tracking capacity) that make scalability testing of stateful gateways possible.
publications.edge_relevance: Software-Defined Networks and 5G (Computer Networks and Communications)

department: Graduate School of Information Science and Technology
research_summary: Leader of Japan's legendary WIDE Project. Pioneer of IPv6, smart building operating systems, and distributed IoT edge infrastructures.
edge_relevance: Focuses on building-scale and campus-scale edge orchestration, IoT data hubs, and cyber-physical energy systems.
research_trajectory: From IPv6 protocol standardization to smart city edge platforms and digital twin network synchronization.

publications.title: A multipath redundancy communication framework for enhancing 5G mobile communication quality
publications.research_problem: 5G quality varies by place and time, and most reliability work targets TCP rather than real-time UDP streaming.
publications.approach: A multipath redundant communication framework that sends real-time media over two mobile networks, tested from a moving vehicle in a city.
publications.key_contribution: Better real-time WebRTC streaming quality over commercial 5G through multipath redundancy.
publications.edge_relevance: Advanced Wireless Network Optimization (Electrical and Electronic Engineering)

publications.title: DIPA2: An Image Dataset with Cross-cultural Privacy Perception Annotations
publications.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive Mobile Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies
publications.research_problem: There is little data on which image content people perceive as privacy-threatening, or how this differs across cultures.
publications.approach: An open image dataset with object-level annotations of information type, perceived severity and intended sharing scope from annotators of different cultures.
publications.key_contribution: DIPA2: 5,897 privacy annotations covering 3,347 objects in 1,304 images.
publications.edge_relevance: Privacy, Security, and Data Protection (Sociology and Political Science)

publications.title: Addressing the Gap Between Training Data and Deployed Environment by On-Device Learning
publications.research_problem: TinyML accuracy degrades after deployment because of noise, sensor placement and drift that were absent from the training data.
publications.approach: Neural-network on-device learning that retrains in the field through semi-supervised sequential training, implemented on Raspberry Pi Pico wireless sensor nodes.
publications.key_contribution: Higher anomaly-detection accuracy in noisy environments, with lower communication and energy cost for battery-powered IoT devices.
publications.edge_relevance: Air Quality Monitoring and Forecasting (Environmental Engineering)

publications.title: BOTAN: BOnd TArgeting Network for prediction of slow glassy dynamics by machine learning relative motion
publications.research_problem: Machine-learning models of glassy dynamics usually learn a single dynamic quantity, limiting insight into slow structural relaxation.
publications.approach: BOTAN, a graph neural network that learns the relative motion of neighbouring particle pairs as well as each particle's own motion.
publications.key_contribution: High-precision prediction of how slow structural relaxation develops in space and time.

publications.key_contribution: Topology-independent decentralised clustering for scalable hierarchical routing, beyond the simple grid networks handled previously.

publications.title: GAMPALv2: An Anomaly Detection Mechanism for Internet Traffic by Predicting Flow Size Range from Time Features
publications.venue: IEICE Transactions on Information and Systems
publications.research_problem: The earlier GAMPAL backbone anomaly detector was computationally heavy, had hard-to-set thresholds and could not pinpoint when and where anomalies occurred.
publications.approach: GAMPALv2 reduces input dimensionality with time features and replaces the LSTM with a random-forest regressor that predicts flow-size ranges per prefix aggregate.
publications.key_contribution: A practical, label-free backbone traffic anomaly detector that resolves GAMPAL's three limitations.
publications.edge_relevance: Network Security and Intrusion Detection (Computer Networks and Communications)

publications.title: Qsync: Making Simplified SMR Protocol Tolerant to Partial Network Partitioning
publications.venue: IEICE Transactions on Information and Systems
publications.research_problem: The Rabia state-machine-replication protocol can livelock under partial network partitions because replica queue states diverge.
publications.approach: Qsync adds queue-state synchronisation to Rabia while keeping its simple design.
publications.key_contribution: Stable throughput under partial partitions in which the original Rabia's throughput drops to zero.
publications.edge_relevance: Mobile Agent-Based Network Management (Computer Networks and Communications)
